knowledge-base.overview: Next.js 14+ (App Router) guardrails, routing conventions, Server vs Client Component rules, data fetching strategies, Server Actions, API route handlers, middleware, and deployment patterns. Applies to TypeScript-first full-stack Next.js applications.

core-principles.principle: All components in app/ are Server Components unless marked 'use client'. Default to server; add client only when required.
Fetch data in the component that needs it. Avoid prop-drilling fetched data through multiple layers.
Server handles data and SEO; Client handles interactivity. Push 'use client' as low in the tree as possible.
Prefer Server Actions for form submissions and mutations. Reserve API route handlers for external consumers or webhooks.
Validate all inputs with Zod in Server Actions and API routes. Never trust raw FormData or request bodies.

guardrail.rule: Never import server-only modules (database clients, secrets, fs) in Client Components. This leaks secrets to the browser bundle.
guardrail.bad: 'use client'; import { db } from '@/lib/db'; // BLOCKER: db runs server-side only

guardrail.rule: Push 'use client' as low in the component tree as possible. Mark only the interactive leaf that needs state or browser APIs — not its parent layout or page.
Validate all Server Action inputs with Zod before processing. Raw FormData must never reach the database unparsed.
Validate all API route handler inputs with Zod. Return typed error responses for validation failures (400) and unexpected errors (500).
Fetch independent data in parallel with Promise.all. Never chain sequential awaits for unrelated fetches in the same component.
guardrail.bad: const user = await getUser(id); const orders = await getOrders(id); // sequential — slow

guardrail.rule: Implement loading.tsx and error.tsx for every route segment that performs data fetching. Do not leave segments without loading and error states.
Use Suspense boundaries to stream slow data. Never block the entire page on one slow fetch when other content can render first.
Set proper metadata on every page for SEO. Use generateMetadata for dynamic pages. Every page.tsx must have either a static metadata export or generateMetadata function.
Use next/image for all images and next/font for fonts. These enforce performance best practices (lazy loading, CLS prevention, font optimization) automatically.
Use Server Actions for form mutations instead of API routes. Server Actions work without client JavaScript for basic submissions and integrate with the React form model.
Choose the correct fetch caching strategy for each endpoint. Defaulting to force-cache when data changes frequently causes stale UIs.
Never expose secrets in API response bodies or error messages in production. Return generic error messages and log detailed context server-side.

routing.description: App Router uses file-system conventions. Every file name has a specific role.

file-conventions.file: Route UI — makes the segment publicly accessible
Shared layout that wraps children and persists across navigations
Automatic Suspense boundary — shown while page/layout loads
API route handler (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH)
Like layout but re-mounts on each navigation

routing.route-patterns: app/ ├── page.tsx # / ├── about/page.tsx # /about ├── blog/ │ ├── page.tsx # /blog │ └── [slug]/page.tsx # /blog/:slug (dynamic) ├── shop/ │ └── [...categories]/page.tsx # /shop/a/b/c (catch-all) ├── (marketing)/ # Route group — no URL segment impact │ ├── pricing/page.tsx # /pricing │ └── features/page.tsx # /features └── @modal/ # Parallel route (named slot) └── login/page.tsx

server-vs-client.description: Decision table for choosing Server vs Client components.

composition-pattern.description: Fetch data in Server Components, pass to Client Components as props. Never pass functions or class instances as props across the server/client boundary.

caching-options.option: Static — default for GET, cached indefinitely

server-actions.description: Server Actions run on the server, integrate with React forms, and work without client JS for basic submissions. Use for all mutations.

api-routes.description: API route handlers for external consumers, webhooks, or when full HTTP semantics are needed. File: app/api/[resource]/route.ts

middleware.description: Edge middleware runs before every matched request. Use for auth checks, redirects, A/B testing, and request header manipulation. Located at project root as middleware.ts.

quick-reference.item: 'use client' at top of file — push as low as possible
'use server' in actions.ts or inline Server Action
Colocate with component; use Promise.all for parallel fetches
Suspense with skeleton fallback per slow section
Server Actions for forms; API routes for external consumers
Zod in every Server Action and API route handler
Every page.tsx exports metadata or generateMetadata
middleware.ts at project root with config.matcher
